groups.label: Throughput and deadlines
groups.blurb: Where operational work loses time, and what to change.

projects.title: Appeals Friction Radar
projects.q: Where does an appeal actually lose its days?
projects.finding: The queue with the tightest deadline is the one that misses it. Urgent appeals take 15.5 days against a 7-day target; standard appeals take 14.8 against 30. Stage dwell time measured with SQL window functions.

projects.title: Case Assignment Fairness
projects.q: Are some teams slower, or are they handed harder work?
projects.finding: A 25.9%–84.2% spread across teams looked like a performance gap. It was routing: 14% of cases produced 41% of all lateness. This reversed the stakeholder's starting hypothesis.

projects.title: Capacity-to-Deadline Optimizer
projects.q: Can cancelled slots be refilled from the waitlist in time?
projects.finding: Reminders cut no-shows from 15.7% to 5.3%. Found 507 refillable cancelled slots and ranked 1,786 waitlisted patients against them with a match score, so a scheduler knows who to call.

groups.label: Dollars and data trust
groups.blurb: Where money leaks, and whether the numbers can be trusted.

projects.title: Denial Prevention Simulator
projects.q: Which denials were preventable before the claim went out?
projects.finding: Of $5.42M denied, $4.48M — 82.7% of denied dollars — traces to five causes checkable at submission. Turned that into a pre-submission risk queue that scores claims before they leave.

projects.title: KPI Trust Ledger
projects.q: Why does the same KPI have four different values?
projects.finding: Backlog reported as 423 / 611 / 509 / 211 depending on which system you asked. Attributed every variance, certified 2 of 6 KPIs for leadership use, and documented exactly why the other four could not be.

groups.label: Beyond healthcare
groups.blurb: The same method applied to retention, experimentation and fraud — because it is a method, not a domain.

projects.title: Subscription Churn and Retention
projects.q: Which acquisition channel keeps customers, and is that the channel's fault?
projects.finding: Paid Social retained 51.2% at month 6 against Member Referral's 78.3% — a 27-point spread. Standardising on discount mix narrows it to 20.3 points, so a quarter of the “channel gap” is a discounting decision, not a channel.

projects.title: Funnel Conversion and Experiment Readout
projects.q: The A/B test won by 4.28 points. Should it ship?
projects.finding: Ship to desktop, not mobile — and not because mobile lost. The headline is a +8.81pp desktop win diluted by a mobile result that was never powered to detect it. Mobile is inconclusive, not null.

metrics.l: days a peek would have called it

projects.title: Chargeback Screening
projects.q: The chargeback rate looks like it fell 74%. Did it?
projects.finding: No — disputes arrive up to 120 days late. Once maturity is respected, a ranked queue catches 123 disputes against the rule engine's 67 at identical analyst cost. McNemar p<0.001. The threshold, though, should not move.
